title: Ian Fleming's Jamaica Routine for Writing James Bond Novels
summary: Ian Fleming wrote all 14 James Bond novels following a structured yet relaxed daily schedule at his Goldeneye home in Jamaica. It kicked off at 7:30 a.m. with a swim and breakfast, included two focused writing blocks totaling 2,000 words with no editing, plus lobster snorkeling, pink gins, a siesta, garden time, and evenings with strong drinks, dinner, and Scrabble with his wife Ann before bed at 10 p.m. He credited this routine, shared in a 1964 Playboy interview, for finishing a novel draft in six weeks each winter, blending discipline with tropical leisure that many now admire for its balance of work and joy.
hook: Picture starting your day with an ocean swim, then crafting 007 adventures amid snorkeling and siestas at a Jamaican estate.

title: Practical Habits Help People with ADHD Thrive Daily
summary: The post by @Squeeze1i outlines habits like never trusting memory, writing everything down instantly, and using visible sticky notes, alarms, and lists to externalize tasks. Users agree these tools are lifesavers, adding their own tips like high-visibility notes on phones or doors, minimalism to cut choices, and accountability buddies. Many note the strategies work for everyone, aligning with expert advice on compensating for working memory challenges through environmental supports.
hook: A simple thread listing everyday strategies for managing ADHD has struck a chord, with people sharing how notes and alarms keep their lives on track without big changes.

title: Do Ultra-Successful People Need Hobbies Beyond Work?
summary: Her post prompted a lively back-and-forth, with some agreeing that work passion crowds out traditional leisure, like Matt Paulson who turns side interests into ventures. Others pushed back, like Milly Tamati who built her company to make time for food growing and fermenting, and Tanner Alexander who prioritizes a full life over ultra-success. Research adds nuance, showing entrepreneurs with day jobs succeed more often, and Nobel scientists with creative pursuits outperform peers, while many CEOs credit hobbies for better energy and ideas.
hook: Executive coach Dr. Julie Gurner shared a bold observation: every very successful person she works with treats business as their hobby, with little room for anything else.

title: Monday Exhaustion Hits Hard with Social Jetlag Blues
summary: People shared their struggles with sleep slumps, early wake-ups, and groggy naps that left them worse off, turning timelines into a shared vent about the workweek start. This matches social jetlag, where weekend sleep shifts mess with the body's clock, leading to extra fatigue and mood dips on Mondays. Data shows 70% feel tired then, with shorter sleep and more grogginess than other days, as users swapped empathy, tips, and memes of slumped shoulders.
hook: One user wished everyone a good morning—except themselves—longing to burrow back under the covers on this dragging October Monday.

title: Why We Endure Hated Jobs But Ditch New Businesses Fast
summary: Justin Welsh pointed out how people show endless patience for miserable jobs but zero for businesses they just launched, paired with a meme of someone puzzled by their own impulse buys. Traders chimed in, saying patience is their real edge in volatile markets, even if it lacks the thrill of quick wins—unlike sticking with hated careers for steady pay. Data backs it up: 22% of new U.S. businesses close in year one, half by year five, while many workers linger in unsatisfying roles for benefits and stability. The chat urges giving personal ventures the same long runway we grant bad bosses.
hook: Ever stuck in a job you can't stand for years, yet bail on your own startup after a few rough months? A sharp post nails this quirky human habit, sparking nods from traders and founders alike.

title: Mark Cuban Advises Taking Any Job to Build a Career
summary: In a clip from the Diary of a CEO podcast, the billionaire tells paycheck-to-paycheck workers to grab any job available, excel at it with brutal self-honesty, and let strong performance create opportunities—even from fast-food gigs within two to three years. Many praise the practical push to prove value and build references, while critics say it ignores a tough job market where effort doesn't always lead to advancement or fair rewards. The advice has fueled wide-ranging talks on ambition, steady work, and economic realities today.
hook: Mark Cuban cuts through the noise with simple words for anyone scraping by: skip chasing the perfect job and just get to work.

title: Revolut Founder Shares Lessons on Defying Investors and Crushing Competition
summary: In a recent podcast, Revolut's founder Nik Storonsky explained how he removed all VCs from the board after rejecting pressure to axe a top 'hardcore' employee, favoring operators who build businesses. He stressed founder-led intensity beats professional CEOs, praised China's grueling work culture for survival, and noted only a handful of co-working startups endure by working weekends. The strategy fueled Revolut's $6 billion revenue in 2025 and rapid customer growth, aiming to top banks in 100 countries.
hook: Nik Storonsky once stared down an investor urging him to fire a star employee—and kept the team intact, paving Revolut's path to $115 billion success.

title: Posts Share Wisdom on Breaking the Overthinking Habit
summary: Users posted lines like 'OVER THINKING NO DEY SOLVE PROBLEM' and 'Overthinking isn’t thinking too much. It’s thinking without deciding,' capturing frustration with rumination that fuels anxiety without solutions. One quip asked, 'if you can overthink the worst, why can’t you overthink the best?' while another balanced it as 'big overthinker but also big idgafer.' Cleveland Clinic experts back this with tips like daily worry periods, grounding exercises, and reframing thoughts into actionable plans to choose peace over endless loops.
hook: A simple book excerpt about overthinking creating nonexistent problems struck a chord, sparking shares of raw advice and funny confessions from everyday folks.

title: Harry Kane's Ballon d’Or Post Draws Mixed Reactions
summary: On October 26, England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane posted the motivational message after winning the men's Ballon d’Or, quickly gaining over a million likes as supporters praised it as a nod to his persistent career path. Some echoed the words exactly, seeing his trophy as proof of quiet dedication. A Dutch journalist's story of a pre-voting exclusive interview offer from Kane's team led others to question the timing, highlighting award-season tensions between promotion and humility. Fans largely stand by Kane's on-field record amid the ongoing back-and-forth.
hook: Harry Kane stood tall with the 2026 Ballon d’Or in London, then shared a simple motto: 'Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise.' Fans loved it, but not everyone agreed.

title: Readers Admit PDFs and Books Often Go Unread
summary: The post claimed nobody finishes PDF books, drawing nods from many who prefer the feel of physical pages with their smell and satisfying turns. Others confessed even bought books sit unread for years, while a few defended screen reading for late-night sessions or research. Data shows over half of American adults haven't completed a full book in the past year, highlighting how digital access mixes good intentions with distractions.
hook: Ever downloaded a PDF with big plans to read it, only for it to gather digital dust? A simple claim on X struck a chord, as readers shared their unfinished stories.

title: AI Automates Brain Work Faster Than Physical Jobs, Echoing Moravec’s Paradox
summary: Hossenfelder pointed out that cognitive tasks like theoretical physics and economics face faster AI competition than physical jobs constrained by regulations and reality. This aligns with Moravec’s paradox from 1988, where machines handle abstract reasoning more easily than human-like sensorimotor skills, as reinforced by recent Epoch AI analyses. Commenters like software engineer Ivana noted AI amplifies those already skilled, while real-world examples show AI agents uncovering hidden scientific insights in weeks, from health policy to biology—prompting talks on adaptation over replacement.
hook: Physicist Sabine Hossenfelder shared a sharp observation: truck driving faces real-world hurdles to automation, while coding and math yield quickly to AI's strengths.

title: Designers Debate AI's Power to Elevate or Flood Creativity
summary: On X, many argue AI boosts design by handling patterns and conventions, letting skilled creators speed up workflows without replacing human craft—much like solving tough math problems. Critics counter that it churns out generic, low-effort content, echoing concerns from Canadian graphic design students about poor hierarchy and a 'sea of sameness.' Data shows graphic design jobs declining per the World Economic Forum, yet the UK design economy grew to £136.7 billion in 2023, supporting calls to blend expertise with AI for standout results.
hook: Designers are pushing back against calling AI work 'slop,' seeing it instead as a tool that lifts everyday design standards while sparking real worries about job shifts.

title: Yale Economist Models Labor's Decline in AGI Future
summary: In 'We Won't Be Missed: Work and Growth in the AGI World,' Restrepo theorizes that advanced AI automating bottleneck tasks would make output depend on compute, not labor, driving wages toward zero as labor's GDP share fades. Accessory human roles might linger for non-efficiency reasons, but pay would match AI replication costs. Online reactions mix fears of concentrated power with hopes for adaptations like basic income, capital ownership, and new income paths in a post-labor economy.
hook: Imagine a world where AI handles all essential work, leaving human wages tied to the cost of running machines. Yale economist Pascual Restrepo's paper sketches this stark possibility.

title: Sabine Hossenfelder Predicts AI Will Reshape Pure Intelligence Work First
summary: She explained that fields like theoretical physics and economics will follow, as AI mines scientific literature to spot overlooked insights and potentially trigger a second scientific revolution. While stock markets buzz with excitement, she noted top AI models might stay exclusive to big institutions. The discussion drew parallels to J.C.R. Licklider's 1960 vision of human-computer symbiosis, where machines handle routine tasks and people guide the big picture, with users adding nuance on physical delays and AI's edge in abstract domains.
hook: Sabine Hossenfelder shared a clear-eyed take on October 27: AI will hit coding and math hardest, sifting through vast spaces faster than humans ever could.

title: Tech Workers Split on AI: Experimenters Gain, Others Lag
summary: A clear divide is emerging between tech workers who independently experiment with AI tools and boost their efficiency, and those frustrated by a lack of management guidance as they watch peers pull ahead. Lists of 50 practical AI tools for writing, coding, images, and automation are helping skilled users work smarter, with data from PwC and ZipRecruiter showing faster growth in AI-exposed companies and higher productivity for proactive adopters. Optimism prevails that AI rewards those blending core skills with tools, though concerns linger about job shifts and the need for retraining.
hook: In tech, some professionals are transforming their jobs with AI experiments, while others feel stuck waiting for bosses to show the way.

title: AI Agents Divide Tech Workers by Adaptation Mindset
summary: A clear split shows in responses to powerful AI agents handling coding and complex tasks: experienced engineers see exciting opportunities in higher-level skills like system architecture and judgment, while some feel frustrated and envious without guidance. Adaptable workers combining tech know-how with storytelling and business savvy gain the most leverage, as companies scale AI without shrinking teams—90% of U.S. tech leaders report maintaining or growing headcount amid higher output. The discussion highlights how initiative and mindset determine success in this evolving landscape.
hook: Technical pros mourn their coding skills fading, while others eagerly reinvent workflows to thrive with AI tools.

title: AI Coding Agents Speed Up Output But Widen Verification Gap
summary: A Harvard study of millions of work events shows AI coding agents boosted lines of code per worker by 30 percent and pull requests by 23 percent, yet review times jumped 49 percent with no gains in completed tasks. Engineers on X debate solutions like automating reviews with AI, generating tests and docs first, and layering human judgment on top, while keeping eyes on critical areas like payments. Tools like OVI aim to help by running reviews, tests, and reports that understand the product, signaling a shift where verification—not writing code—is now the real challenge.
hook: Software teams love how AI agents crank out code faster than ever. But with review times ballooning, engineers are scrambling to verify it all without slowing down.

title: Developers Debate AI's Role in Easing Game Coding Drudgery
summary: A discussion highlights that 90% of game coding involves tough, repetitive tasks like fighting compilers and fixing bugs, while AI tools could handle that load to free humans for imagination and decisions. Builders note AI already speeds up scripts, data generation, and routine fixes, though understanding and maintaining the code remains key. While some worry AI might eventually touch creative work, most see it as a helpful collaborator that cuts toil without replacing human judgment.
hook: Game developers are sharing how much of their work feels like endless bug hunts and compiler battles, with just a small slice left for the fun, creative parts.

title: Developers Debate If AI Outcodes Humans Forever
summary: The discussion highlights AI's strengths in tasks like bug-spotting and code generation, with benchmarks placing models like Claude Opus 5.5 at the top. Developers like Ivana and Riley Brown emphasize building real skills first, such as manual video editing or questioning AI's simplistic fixes that ignore deeper architecture. Figures like Yann LeCun and Eric Schmidt note AI amplifies human work rather than replacing it, pushing engineers toward better system design, prompting, and oversight.
hook: Arpit Bhayani's bold claim on October 25—that no human will ever code better than large language models—drew over 15,000 likes and sparked hundreds of thoughtful replies from fellow developers.

title: Experts Get Most Value from AI in Game Development
summary: A discussion highlighted that people with strong expertise in tasks like game development prompt AI most effectively, using their knowledge to guide outputs and avoid pitfalls. Users agreed fundamentals prevent errors and unlock potential, while concerns linger over AI's speed disadvantaging years of human effort in projects. A VAIA study shows 94% of game studios now integrate AI for coding, concepts, and prototyping, with recent tools adding multiview 3D and character motion features as of October 27.
hook: Ivana's blunt take landed hard: those thriving with AI in creative fields already know how to create without it. The conversation unpacked how deep skills turn tools into real amplifiers.

title: Tesla Opens Job Postings for Vietnam Entry with Sales and Service Team
summary: After registering a subsidiary in Ho Chi Minh City on September 11 with $3 million in capital, Tesla shared five key openings: Sales Manager, Service Manager, HR Business Partner, Purchasing Manager, and Project Developer for Charging. Recruiter Ricky Ip announced the hires on X, emphasizing the mission to create abundance with passionate locals. The roles signal plans for retail, service operations, and a Supercharger network in Vietnam's fast-growing EV market, where VinFast leads but Tesla eyes customer experience amid import challenges. No launch details yet, but reactions show excitement for test drives and official service.
hook: Tesla is building its first team in Vietnam, posting jobs for sales managers and charging experts to bring official support to eager drivers.

title: No Millennials Left in Their 20s by End of 2026
summary: Pew Research defines Millennials as those born from 1981 to 1996, shaped by events like 9/11 and the internet's rise. By December 2026, the youngest hit 30, leaving Gen Z as the only generation in their 20s. Online reactions blend humor—like a 1995 baby comparing it to LeBron's prime—with nostalgia and critiques of mismatched images, such as Gen X's Friends cast representing them.
hook: The clock is ticking down on the final 20-something Millennials, born 1981 to 1996, as they all turn 30 or older this year.

title: Jesse Ventura Calls Trump Coward Over Vietnam Draft Dodging
summary: Ventura expressed deep frustration that Trump avoided the Vietnam War with bone spurs—a condition that 'never stopped him from golf,' he quipped—despite Ventura's own 17 months in Southeast Asia alongside his brother. The interview also delved into Ventura's longstanding questions about 9/11, including witness accounts of no plane at the Pentagon and odd details like 'toasted cars,' leaving Piker visibly uncomfortable. Viewers split on the exchange, with some praising Ventura's military candor and others pointing to Trump's defiant 'Fight!' response after the 2024 assassination attempt.
hook: Jesse Ventura, the Navy veteran and former governor, leaned in during his Minneapolis chat with Hasan Piker and unloaded on Donald Trump for dodging Vietnam while he and his brother served two tours.

title: Millennials Share Burnout Stories from Constant Survival Mode
summary: Many in the generation describe following the rules—college, steady jobs, overtime—yet facing nonstop survival mode with mounting bills and little security. A Deloitte report shows 45% report burnout, driven by financial stress, while a Business Insider analysis notes they're 'stability stacking' through side hustles after economic shocks. Personal stories highlight frustrations like working nonstop without family safety nets, with some calling the system a scam and dreaming of simpler lives, though Gen X voices note similar long-term struggles.
hook: A video explaining why Millennials born 1981-1996 feel exhausted in 2026 struck a chord, drawing waves of personal tales about endless bills and job struggles.

title: Gen Z Thriving Rating Hits Record Low in 2026 Gallup Poll
summary: Gallup's 2026 poll reveals only 44% of adults born 1997-2012 rate their lives as thriving on the Life Evaluation Index, down from 64% in 2010, while Millennials have dipped too and Boomers hit a record high of 53% for those 65+. Younger groups aged 18-29 score the lowest at under half, amid rising costs for rent, groceries, gas, and entry-level struggles like an 8.0% unemployment rate for 20-24-year-olds. The report links the decline to depression, weaker social ties, and post-pandemic changes, contrasting with older generations' financial security from home equity and savings.
hook: Fewer than half of Gen Z adults now describe their lives as thriving, a steep fall from just a few years ago. It's a stark shift that spotlights the pressures young people face today.

title: All Millennials Turn 30 or Older by End of 2026
summary: Pew Research defines Millennials as those born 1981 to 1996, a group shaped by the internet's rise and 9/11, now ranging from 30 to 45 years old. People shared everything from pride in their 'golden years' to jokes about aging, with one calling it 'the end of an era' and another noting getting older as a 'privilege.' Gen Z, born 1997 onward, steps up as the new young adults amid the mix of nostalgia and humor.
hook: As 2026 wraps up, the last Millennials born in 1996 hit 30, closing the door on their collective 20s with a wave of online reflections and laughs.

title: Generational Clash Over Economic Struggles Past and Present
summary: A post highlighting today's high costs for Gen Z sparked replies from both sides, with boomers recalling physical jobs, family sacrifices, and no free handouts to build their lives. Younger posters point to stagnant wages, AI job threats, and homes now worth millions that elders bought cheaply, amid data showing older Americans hold 75% of national wealth. Both share real hardships—past eras with brutal labor and few safety nets, today with education debt and housing ratios at historic highs—urging empathy across the divide.
hook: Young adults share stories of $2,500 rents and $60,000 student loans crushing their starts, while older voices counter with tales of low wages and 19% mortgage rates from decades ago.

title: Thai-German Patrick Finkler Wins Hearts with Skateboarding on Chinese Music Show
summary: On '国音正青春,' a China Media Group variety program blending traditional Chinese music with youthful twists, 23-year-old Thai-German performer Patrick Nattawat Finkler—known as 尹浩宇—showcases real skateboarding skills during outdoor segments and group activities. Fans share clips of his cool moves, lighthearted studio chats, and endearing reactions that have them laughing and cooing. The weekly show airs on CCTV-3 and CCTV-15, streaming on 央视频, highlighting cultural exchanges through music with Patrick's international flair drawing growing excitement.
hook: Patrick Finkler glides effortlessly across an outdoor basketball court on his skateboard, hoodie and jeans flying, his sweet smiles and puzzled expressions stealing the show.

title: Endless Cruise Ship Strands Passengers in Cambodia Over Fuel Costs
summary: Villa Vie Odyssey passengers, who paid up to $120,000 for cabins on a multi-year world voyage starting from Belfast in October 2024, were told to disembark in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, after the U.S. operator suspended operations on October 27, 2026. Skyrocketing fuel prices—from $1,800 to $6,000–$8,000 per cabin monthly—tied to the Iran war made continuation impossible despite cuts like slower speeds and longer port stays. The company is arranging temporary lodging and transport while pursuing restructuring over 60 days, but no resumption is guaranteed, leaving retirees and others facing uncertainty ashore.
hook: One couple learned at 6 a.m. they had to pack up and leave by 2 p.m., ending their dream of endless sea living in a blur of hurried goodbyes.

title: 4EVE Lights Up Paris with Electric Set at The A Festival
summary: On October 25, 2026, the T-pop group 4EVE—formed in 2020 by members Mind, Jorin, Taaom, Hannah, Fai, Punch, and Aheye—delivered a high-energy performance at The A Festival. Their setlist packed hits like “Booty Bomb,” “Hot2Hot,” and “Ooh Lala,” with fans raving over standout looks and the reunion of Tata and Punch onstage. The group later thanked Paris supporters for an unforgettable night, boosting their rising international buzz.
hook: Seven Thai stars from 4EVE hit the Paris stage, blending sharp dances and catchy hits that lit up lightsticks and cheers across the Event Center.

title: Financial Planner Rejects Morning Coffee Delay Advice
summary: Boneparth's blunt rejection of expert advice to delay caffeine—meant to align with natural cortisol rises—struck a chord, as people shared photos of immediate morning brews alongside banana toast, to-go cups, and cozy setups. Many described coffee as the best part of their day or a quick fix for grogginess, while a few noted stomach risks. Research shows no strong evidence that waiting improves energy for most healthy adults, so coffee lovers keep pouring right away.
hook: Financial planner Douglas A. Boneparth dismissed the idea of waiting 60-90 minutes after waking for coffee with a simple 'No.' His post prompted a flood of personal routines, from groggy wake-ups to cheerful breakfast mugs.

title: Bryan Johnson Advises Making Bedrooms Cold, Dark, and Boring for Better Sleep
summary: The biohacker behind the Blueprint longevity project explained that using the bedroom for multiple activities confuses the brain's sleep cues, a principle called stimulus control. Users shared agreements, like a study showing light exposure raises heart rates and insulin resistance, plus Harvard Health's advice for cool temps around 65–68°F and minimal light or noise. While some posted jokes about prison-like setups or noted challenges in small living spaces, many appreciated the reminder to create rest-focused environments.
hook: Bryan Johnson shared a simple tip: keep your bedroom cold, dark, and boring to signal sleep time to your brain. No office, gym, or movie theater allowed.

title: Apple Watch Data Reveals U.S. State Bedtime Averages Around 11:37 p.m.
summary: Researchers from Brigham and Women’s Hospital and the American Heart Association analyzed 17 million nights of sleep data from over 61,000 Apple Watch users, finding the national bedtime average at 11:37 p.m. and sleep duration at just 6 hours 40 minutes — below the recommended 7 to 9 hours. Most states cluster between 11:20 p.m. and 11:45 p.m., with reactions ranging from shock at the late hours to defenses of evening 'you time' after work. The study notes consistent bedtimes link to better sleep quality, more exercise, and less nighttime waking, though Hawaii's early bedtime still yields only 6.5 hours on average.
hook: Hawaii turns in earliest at 11:06 p.m., while D.C. lingers until 11:56 p.m. — a chart from millions of Apple Watch nights has people rethinking their own routines.

title: Widespread Frustrations with Disrupted Sleep Schedules
summary: People share stories of chaotic sleep, from naps turning into all-night wakefulness to the flipped rhythm of 'day is night and night is day.' These complaints surface as clocks prepare to fall back on Nov. 1, a shift that can worsen internal clock disruptions amid screens, stress, and irregular schedules. Experts like UCLA's Gene Block blame glowing devices for circadian misalignment, while surveys show 30% of U.S. adults get under seven hours of sleep nightly; tips include steady bedtimes and morning light to help reset.
hook: One person summed it up bluntly: 'fucked up my sleep schedule again. fuck.' Countless others echo the exhaustion of feeling sleepy all day but wide awake at night.

title: Late October Wave of Exhaustion Hits Hard
summary: In late October, people are posting about overwhelming tiredness, from being sleepy all day to dreading work and wanting to shut their brains off. Posts like 'I’m so tired both physically and mentally I don’t wanna think at all' pair with visuals of low-battery kittens, Snoopy in the rain, and folks looking utterly spent. Shorter days, poor sleep, and constant demands fuel this shared slump, with many simply counting down to rest.
hook: One person slumped against a concrete wall, another gave a tired thumbs-down from bed—these images capture the deep fatigue many are feeling right now.

title: Many Share Sleep Struggles Amid Autumn Fatigue
summary: On October 27, 2026, people described restless nights, late bedtimes they regretted at dawn, and a general drain that naps couldn't fix. Shorter autumn days mess with internal clocks by cutting daylight, sparking earlier melatonin and lower serotonin that leave folks sluggish. In Europe and the UK, the recent clock change on October 25 adds to the adjustment woes, with some tying it to Halloween excitement too. Experts suggest steady bedtimes, morning light, and less evening screens to ease through it.
hook: Waking up still feeling wiped out, even after a full night's rest—it's a morning many are facing right now.

title: Daylight Saving Time Ends Sunday Amid Heated Permanent Time Debate
summary: Most U.S. states will shift from 2 a.m. daylight saving time to 1 a.m. standard time, marking the return to winter hours after the spring forward. The House passed a bill in July 2026 to make daylight saving permanent year-round, but the Senate let it stall in committee despite President Trump's call for a vote and laws from 19 states waiting on federal approval. While nearly everyone agrees to end the twice-yearly changes, supporters of permanent daylight saving favor extra evening light for activities, but sleep experts push standard time to match natural body rhythms and boost health and safety.
hook: This Sunday, November 1, clocks spring back an hour, delivering brighter mornings but earlier sunsets—and reigniting arguments over whether to ditch the switches forever.

title: Gehlee Dangca's Serene Morning Yoga Captivates PBB Fans
summary: The 19-year-old Filipino singer, known as the Darling K-Pop Idol ng Las Piñas, joined PBB Collab 3.0 after her UNIS debut and recent solo single Closer. Clips of her calm seated stretches and giggles have fans praising her effortless grace and demure energy. Viewers love how she turns simple routines into special moments, with one noting housemate Lans was spot on about her beauty during exercise.
hook: Gehlee Dangca unrolls her purple mat on the PBB lawn, flowing through gentle stretches in a white tee and beige pants. Fans call it a dreamy, serotonin-boosting start to the day.
